scope: PR-cycle diff-based security verdict for the 0.4.6 hotfix lane, re-keyed to head 47cbee92. REVIEWED RANGE: git diff 17043ed4..47cbee92 - 1 commit, 2 files, 17 insertions and 3 deletions. This is the delta on top of the range my previous verdict covered (e354b18c, whose verdict file is deleted with this one written, because a superseded verdict is slop and the directory holds exactly one file). The single commit calibrates the test-suite tier timeout ceiling for coverage instrumentation: tests/conftest.py gains a coverage keyword on the ceiling function and a x2 factor read once at collection from the coverage source option, and the contract test that pins the ceiling table gains 3 assertions. Path classes, proven: git diff --name-only over the range returns 2 paths, both under the tests tree; filtered to the production package 0 paths, to the workflows directory 0 paths, to the dependency manifests and lockfile 0 paths, to the whole specs tree (bug ledger and backlog included) 0 paths. The reviewed question - whether a widened ceiling weakens a security control - is answered no on evidence: the ceiling is a stewardship control, the quarantine discipline and the explicit-timeout override guard are byte-identical across the range, and zero tests are skipped, deleted or quarantined. Three things were executed rather than reasoned about: the coverage-detection path was probed with and without the flag and the applied timeout markers observed directly, the contract suite pinning the ceiling table was run green, and the repository's own locked dependency set was audited. CVE lane: no dependency line in the range, and the lockfile audits clean independently. IaC lane: no workflow, container or Terraform path - no input. Secrets lane: the added lines were swept and are clean. Bug-history lane: the ledger fold is unchanged by this range and the predecessor calibration bug on the same function was examined for the bug-surface axis.
verdict_reason: No CRITICAL, no HIGH and no MEDIUM finding, and none of the mandatory REQUEST_CHANGES triggers is present: no secret or token, no PII, no public-asset privacy violation, no auth or access-control change, no dependency addition, no generated-file leakage, no deploy leakage, no consumer-specific data exposure. The range contains zero production lines. The central question is answered by measurement, not by argument. A per-test tier ceiling caps a runaway test so its failure is attributable; it gates no authentication, authorisation, cryptography, deserialisation, path resolution or secret handling, and the product memory sanctions exactly this shape - security controls fail loudly, non-security features may degrade with bounded, explicit behaviour. Every enforcement seam adjacent to the change is byte-identical across the range: the quarantine discipline that refuses collection of a quarantined test without a registered bug id, the guard that lets an explicit timeout marker win, the closed marker set, and the path-to-marker table. Zero tests are skipped, deleted, xfailed or quarantined by the range. The new input carries no injection surface - it is pytest's own parsed option, coerced to a boolean and used only to select an integer multiplier, never reaching a path, a shell, a subprocess, an eval or a regex. Two properties were proven on the executed path rather than asserted. First, the fail direction is TIGHT: probing collection with no coverage flag, with the flag the CI steps actually pass, and with a bare flag yields ceilings of 10s, 20s and 20s respectively, so every input that is not an active coverage run keeps the original narrower ceiling and no reachable input removes the ceiling or widens it beyond a fixed 2x. Second, the one property a raised ceiling could genuinely damage still holds with margin: the widest ceiling reachable in a coverage job is 180s against a 480s budget on the cross runner and 60s against 300s on ubuntu, so a genuine hang still fails loudly and attributably instead of being cancelled silently at the job level - and the large e2e product is unreachable because no coverage job collects e2e. The tightest ceilings also survive untouched on the two non-coverage fast jobs. The contract suite pinning the ceiling table runs green, 9 passed. The dependency lane carries a measured number rather than an absence argument: the repository's own lockfile audits clean, 0 known vulnerabilities across 74 of 76 locked packages, the 2 exclusions being platform- and interpreter-gated wheels that cannot install on a linux runner. Bug-surface axis (FR24; ledger fold unchanged at this head - 1016 records, 495 distinct ids, exactly 1 unresolved, and git diff over the range touches 0 paths in the bug and backlog ledgers): UNCHANGED for production, since the range contains zero production lines, branches, flags and code paths; CONTAINED for the test tooling. That second half was examined rather than assumed, because this is the second ceiling calibration on the same function and the single unresolved bug at this head is precisely its predecessor. The two causes are genuinely distinct - a slower runner versus tracing overhead on the same runner - they compose multiplicatively, and the fix stays inside the single calibration home the module comment already declares, mirroring the factor already present instead of bolting a second mechanism beside it. The alternative that would have grown the feature - explicit timeout markers sprinkled across affected tests, which the module comment explicitly forbids - was not taken. The function gained one input; the suite gained zero new mechanisms; an opaque worker-crash failure class is replaced by an attributable timeout. The residual items are both LOW and neither is a property of the code under review: a citation that resolves only on another branch's ledger, and advisories in the operator's shared local virtualenv against packages this repository never declares. One structural caveat is recorded rather than blocked on: the ceiling model is fixed constants times environment factors, so a third factor would be the signal to review the model itself rather than add another multiplier.

findings.detail_md:

**Path classes, measured rather than asserted.** `git diff --name-only` over the range, filtered to the production package returns 0 paths; filtered to the workflows directory and container/Terraform shapes, 0 paths; filtered to `pyproject.toml`, the lockfile and `setup.cfg`, 0 paths; filtered to the whole `specs/` tree (bug ledger and backlog included), 0 paths. findings.message: No security control is weakened. The tier ceiling is a stewardship control, and every adjacent enforcement seam in the touched file is byte-identical across the range.
findings.detail_md:
The question this review had to answer is whether widening a timeout weakens anything that gates security. It does not, and the surrounding controls were checked individually rather than waved through:

| control | status in this range | how checked |
|---|---|---|
| Quarantine discipline (`_validate_quarantine_markers`) - a quarantined test without a registered bug id refuses collection | untouched, byte-identical | read + the contract suite passes 9/9 |
| Explicit-timeout override guard (`get_closest_marker("timeout") is None`) | untouched | read; the pre-existing escape hatch is neither widened nor narrowed |
| Closed marker set `_KNOWN_MARKERS` | untouched | read |
| Path-to-marker table `_PATH_MARKERS` | untouched | read |
| Coverage floor (`--cov-fail-under=80`) | untouched | no workflow path in the range |
| Tests skipped, deleted, quarantined or xfailed | zero | grep over added lines returns 0 |

**The ceiling itself.** A per-test timeout caps a runaway test so the failure is attributable. It gates no authentication, authorisation, cryptography, deserialisation, path resolution or secret handling. The product memory states the posture directly: security controls fail loudly when a platform cannot provide them, while non-security features may degrade with an explicit log and bounded behaviour (`specs/memory/product/platform/cross-platform-portability.md`). This is a bounded, documented, centrally calibrated degradation of a non-security control - exactly the sanctioned shape.

**Injection surface of the new input.** `config.option.cov_source` is pytest's own parsed CLI option. It is read through `getattr(..., None)`, immediately coerced with `bool()`, and used only to select an integer multiplier. It never reaches a filesystem path, a shell, a subprocess, an `eval`, a format string, or a regular expression. There is no untrusted-input path here at all.
findings.fix_recommendation: None - the acceptance property holds as reviewed.

findings.message: Coverage detection was proven on the executed path, not reasoned about: the fail direction is TIGHT - every input that is not an active coverage run yields the original, narrower ceiling.
findings.detail_md:
A trylast collection hook was loaded from a scratch directory outside the repository and printed the value the new code reads plus the timeout marker actually applied to collected items. Three invocations against one real unit-test module:

| invocation | `cov_source` observed | ceiling applied to a `unit` item |
|---|---|---|
| no coverage flag | `[]` (falsy) | 10s - unchanged from before the range |
| `--cov=<production package>` - what all three CI coverage steps pass | `['<package>']` (truthy) | 20s |
| bare `--cov` | `[True]` (truthy) | 20s |

**Why the fail direction matters.** The worry with a `getattr`-based feature probe is a fail-open: an input that silently disables the control. Here the opposite holds. If pytest-cov is absent the attribute does not exist, `getattr` returns `None`, `bool()` is false, and the ceiling stays at its original, tighter value. If coverage is requested with no source the list is empty and the ceiling again stays tight. No reachable input removes the ceiling or widens it beyond a fixed 2x of the platform-adjusted base; the `None` return remains reachable only for a non-tier marker, exactly as before the range.

findings.message: The widened ceiling still sits well below every job budget that can reach it, so a genuine hang still produces an attributable per-test timeout instead of an opaque job-level cancellation.
findings.detail_md:
This is the one property a raised ceiling could genuinely damage: if the per-test ceiling exceeded the job budget, a hang would stop failing loudly and start being cancelled silently at the job level. Both coverage jobs were checked against the multiplier table.

| coverage job | runner | job budget | widest ceiling reachable | margin |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ubuntu coverage | linux | 300s | 60s (contract, factor 1 x 2) | 5.0x |
| cross coverage | windows | 480s | 180s (contract, factor 3 x 2) | 2.7x |
| cross coverage | macos | 480s | 60s (darwin has no platform factor) | 8.0x |

The large e2e product (120 x 3 x 2 = 720s) would exceed the 480s cross budget, but it is **unreachable in CI**: both coverage steps select `(unit or contract) and not quarantine` and pass only the unit and contract directories, so no e2e or integration item is ever collected under coverage. The tightest signal also survives elsewhere in the matrix - the two non-coverage fast jobs run without any coverage flag and therefore keep the original 10s and 30s ceilings.
findings.fix_recommendation: None. If an e2e or integration selector is ever added to a coverage job, re-check that product against that job's budget before merging.

findings.message: Dependency lane, measured at head rather than skipped: the repository's own locked dependency set audits clean - 0 known vulnerabilities across 74 of 76 locked packages.

The lockfile was parsed into a pinned requirement set and audited with the pinned-set resolver. Result: **no known vulnerabilities found**, exit 0, across 74 of the 76 locked packages. The 2 excluded entries are platform- or interpreter-gated wheels that cannot install on a linux CPython 3.12 runner (a Windows extension package and a free-threading-only YAML build requiring CPython 3.13); they are excluded because the resolver cannot fetch them here, not because they were waived.

findings.message: Traceability: both new comments cite a bug id that has zero records in this branch's ledger, so the citation does not resolve at this head.
findings.detail_md:
The module comment in `tests/conftest.py` and the assertion comment in `tests/contract/test_stewardship_mechanics.py` both name a bug id describing the coverage-instrumentation ceiling trip. A fold of `specs/bugs/bugs.jsonl` at this head returns **0 records** for that id. The commit subject itself says the record lives in the next release's ledger - that is, on a different branch.

**Why it is only LOW.** No security property depends on it, the ledger is an ADDITIVE path that this range deliberately does not touch, and the hotfix lane legitimately splits registration from the branch carrying the fix. But the workspace law asks a bug fix to carry a checkable lineage line, and an auditor folding this branch alone cannot resolve the citation - the evidence is only reachable if the reader already knows to look at another branch's ledger.

**Not a REQUEST_CHANGES trigger.** It is not a secret, not PII, not an access-control gap, not a dependency addition, not generated-file or deploy leakage, and not consumer-specific data exposure.
findings.fix_recommendation: Operator decision: either append the reported/resolved pair for this id to this branch's ledger, or accept that the hotfix lane's lineage resolves only after the branches converge - and record which, so the next audit does not re-raise it.

findings.message: Bug-surface axis: this is the SECOND ceiling calibration on the same function, and its predecessor is the single unresolved bug in the ledger at this head. Contained here, but a third calibration would mean the ceiling model itself is wrong.
findings.detail_md:
**Ledger fold at this head** (1016 records, 495 distinct ids, terminal events resolved/closed/superseded/deferred/rejected/archived): exactly **1** bug has no terminal event - and it is `windows-xdist-workers-crash-on-unit-fast-tier`, whose fix introduced the platform factor that this range now multiplies. Same file, same function, same table, second calibration, predecessor still open. Repetition on one surface is the operator's stated tripwire for a prior symptom patch, so it was examined rather than noted.

**Assessment: the repetition is legitimate and the diff does not grow the feature.**

- The two causes are genuinely different - a slower runner versus tracing overhead on the same runner - and they compose multiplicatively, which is why one factor cannot express both.
- The fix stays inside the single calibration home the module comment already declares ("one calibration, here, never a per-test marker"). The alternative - sprinkling explicit timeout markers across the affected tests - is precisely the growth this rule forbids, and it was not taken.
- The shape mirrors the factor already present rather than bolting a different mechanism beside it: one module constant, one keyword parameter, one multiplication, one collection-time read. No new code path elsewhere, no flag threaded through call sites, no cross-feature reach-in, no new shared mutable state.
- Direction: **production bug surface unchanged** (0 production lines in the range); **test-tooling surface contained** - the function gained one input, the suite gained zero new mechanisms, and an opaque worker-crash failure class is removed from the coverage jobs in favour of an attributable timeout.

**The structural caveat, for the record.** The model is fixed constants multiplied by environment factors, so each newly discovered environment costs one more factor. Two factors is still a table; a third would be the signal that a measured or adaptive budget is the structural answer rather than another multiplier.
findings.fix_recommendation: No change requested for this PR. Record the tripwire: if a third environment factor is ever proposed for this function, route it to an architecture review of the ceiling model instead of adding the factor. Separately, the still-open predecessor bug wants a terminal event once this lands.

findings.message: Environment hygiene, outside the diff: the shared local workspace virtualenv carries packages with published advisories that this repository never declares or locks. Operator-facing only - no consumer or production exposure.
findings.detail_md:
Auditing the local workspace virtualenv (as opposed to the repository's lockfile) reports advisories against an imaging library, the installer, and the packaging tool. **None of those three appears in this repository's declared dependencies or its lockfile** - verified by grep against both files, which return no match. They are ambient contents of the operator's shared local runtime, which additionally has one locally installed package that does not exist on the public index and therefore cannot be audited at all.

**Scope boundary, stated plainly.** This is not a property of the commit under review, not a property of this repository at this head, and not shipped to any consumer - the published artifact resolves the lockfile audited clean above. It is recorded because a security report that silently discards a real scanner result is not a report; it is not routed as a blocking finding because nothing in the PR touches it.
findings.fix_recommendation: Operator decision, off the PR path: refresh the local workspace virtualenv's installer and packaging tool, and drop or upgrade the imaging library if nothing in the local toolchain needs it. No repository change is implied.

findings.message: Secrets lane clean: zero matches across the range, and the one private-key-shaped match in the tracked tree is a pre-existing truncated synthetic fixture, untouched by this range.
findings.detail_md:
**Range sweep.** The added lines were swept for credential-assignment shapes (password/secret/token/api key/private key/credential/bearer forms) and for dangerous sinks (`eval`, `exec`, subprocess construction, shell execution, pickle, unsafe YAML load, dynamic import, outbound HTTP). Both sweeps return **0 matches**. The range adds no literal value of any kind - only an integer constant, a keyword parameter, and a boolean read.

**Tracked-tree sweep.** A credential-assignment sweep across tracked files outside the archive and the ledger returns 0 matches. One file matches the private-key block pattern: a unit test that writes a deliberately truncated placeholder PEM as a fixture. It is not a key, it carries no material, it is not in this range, and `git diff --name-only` over the range confirms it is untouched.

No value in this report is redacted because no value in the range required redaction.
